item.title: Darknet Forums Are Fragmenting as Observed Breach Activity Rises
item.dc:creator: raphaelge@checkpoint.com
item.description:
Repeated takedowns have disrupted some of the cybercrime underground’s established gathering places. The communities around them have continued to reorganize. BreachForums revivals compete with clones and alternative platforms. Russian-speaking forums have struggled to replace the relationships built around XSS and RAMP. Activity moves between venues, and a platform that gains attention after one disruption may lose it after the next. Check Point Exposure Management researchers examined two years of forum activity to understand how that disruption has changed the underground. The analysis found a more fragmented ecosystem, with observed breach and data-leak activity remaining substantial even as established forums lost […]

item.title: Volant Manticore: New Iranian Threat Group Expands Cyber Espionage Across Europe and the Middle East
item.dc:creator: raphaelge@checkpoint.com
item.description:
Check Point Research has uncovered Volant Manticore, a previously undocumented Iran-nexus threat group that made Cyprus a primary espionage target before recently expanding its operations also to Saudi Arabia. This group’s focus provides another indication that Iranian cyber activity is becoming more geographically distributed, with targeting increasingly shaped by changing geopolitical priorities across the Middle East and Europe. That change in focus is one of the most important parts of the discovery. It shows how quickly Volant Manticore’s targeting can respond to geopolitical developments and adds to evidence that Iranian cyber interests are extending beyond their traditional focus. item.title: New PHP Vulnerabilities: What Organizations Need to Know and How Check Point Customers Are Protected
item.dc:creator: anap@checkpoint.com
item.description:
On November 19, 2026, A series of recently disclosed vulnerabilities in PHP has put one of the world’s most widely deployed web technologies under renewed scrutiny.  The most significant issues, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are critical remote code execution vulnerabilities that can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code on vulnerable PHP systems. CVE-2026-109618 carries a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 and has since been added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.   A third issue, CVE-2026-115560, was disclosed shortly afterward. It involves a more specific PHP configuration and should be considered separately from the two original PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. Public reporting […]

item.title: Ransomware Reaches Record Highs in Q3 2026 as the Threat Landscape Fragments
item.dc:creator: raphaelge@checkpoint.com
item.description:
The State of Ransomware Q3 2026 reveals a combination the ransomware market has not seen before: record victim numbers alongside record-low concentration among its leading groups. More ransomware brands claimed victims, the top ten fell below half of observed activity, and several high-profile organizations rejected major extortion demands. Together, these shifts reveal a ransomware ecosystem growing in volume, spreading across more operators, and facing changes in how victims respond to extortion. Key takeaways Q3 reached a record 2,830 victims, including 964 in July, 1,042 in August and 824 in September. 117 ransomware brands claimed victims, up from 91 in Q2, […]

item.title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): Check Your Java Services Now
item.dc:creator: raphaelge@checkpoint.com
item.description:
What we see   The flaw: On recent Intel and AMD x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI, Java’s hand-tuned Base64 decoder miscalculates the output length for the padded tail of a short malformed input. The result is a write of 62 or 63 bytes past the end of its buffer, depending on the padding. Java rejects the input, but only after the write.   The impact: The bytes written are fixed, so on its own the overflow usually crashes Java.
